findings.title: CLI dispatcher is a god-function with hardcoded command registry
findings.description: src/cli.ts contains a 60+ entry CLI_ONLY Set and a giant switch/if-else chain in handleCliOnly that hardcodes every command name and its dynamic import path. Adding a command requires touching 3+ places (CLI_ONLY set, handleCliOnly switch, help text). This violates open-closed principle and is the single largest architectural debt in the dispatch layer — operations are otherwise discoverable via the operations registry, but CLI-only commands aren't.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a command registry pattern: each command module exports a CommandSpec { name, needsEngine, handler, help } and a barrel file aggregates them. Replace the switch with a Map lookup, mirroring the existing operations registry pattern. This eliminates the CLI_ONLY Set and the duplicated import boilerplate.

findings.title: MCP server imports core operations directly, bypassing a transport boundary
findings.description: src/mcp/server.ts imports `operations` from '../core/operations.ts' and the dispatch helpers from './dispatch.ts'. The 'backward compat' handleToolCall in server.ts duplicates dispatch logic (validateParams + buildOperationContext + op.handler) that already exists in dispatch.ts. This couples the MCP transport to operation internals and creates two code paths for tool invocation (`gbrain call` vs MCP stdio) that can drift.
findings.recommendation: Collapse handleToolCall into a single call to dispatchToolCall with { remote: false }. The MCP server should only know about transport (stdio, HTTP) and delegate ALL execution to dispatch.ts. Move operations import out of server.ts entirely.

findings.title: Command layer reaches into MCP transport (cross-layer dependency)
findings.description: src/commands/call.ts imports handleToolCall from '../mcp/server.ts'. This inverts the expected layering: commands should depend on core (operations, engine), not on a transport adapter. The MCP server should depend on operations, and `gbrain call` should also dispatch through operations directly — not through the MCP server module. This creates a circular concern where mcp/ and commands/ are peers but commands/ pulls from mcp/.
findings.recommendation: Refactor `gbrain call` to import dispatchToolCall from src/mcp/dispatch.ts (or better: a renamed src/core/dispatch.ts since dispatch is transport-agnostic). Move dispatch.ts under src/core/ since it's used by both transport adapters and CLI commands.

findings.title: Auth command bypasses engine abstraction with raw postgres driver
findings.description: src/commands/auth.ts imports `postgres` directly and uses raw SQL via the postgres tagged template, completely bypassing BrainEngine. This means: (a) the command will not work with PGLite brains despite the rest of the system supporting both engines, (b) it duplicates connection/config logic (DATABASE_URL handling) that loadConfig() + engine-factory already solve, and (c) it violates the single point of DB access enforced elsewhere.
findings.recommendation: Refactor auth.ts to receive a BrainEngine and use engine.executeRaw() for the access_tokens CRUD. Either route through cli.ts's connectEngine() or expose a thin AuthRepository in core/ that both engines implement. Remove the direct postgres import.

findings.title: Autopilot reaches into engine internals via 'as any' casts
findings.description: autopilot.ts contains multiple `(engine as any).executeRaw?.(...)` and `(engine as any).connect?.()` calls (lines around the no-worker probe and reconnect block). This bypasses the type system and signals that BrainEngine's interface is incomplete — callers know methods exist but the type doesn't expose them. Coupled with the engine-parity finding, this is evidence that BrainEngine is under-specified as a port.
findings.recommendation: Audit BrainEngine type and add executeRaw, connect, getConfig, getHealth, getCallersOf, getCalleesOf as first-class methods on the interface. Eliminate `as any` casts in command-layer code. If a method is genuinely engine-specific, narrow the type with a discriminated union or keep it private.

findings.title: Operation result formatting hardcoded into CLI with type assertions
findings.description: formatResult() in cli.ts contains a switch with cases for get_page, list_pages, search, query, get_tags, get_stats, get_health, get_timeline, get_versions — each casting result to `any` and reaching into ad-hoc shapes. This couples the CLI to operation result internals without a type contract. New operations require editing this switch; renaming a result field silently breaks formatting.
findings.recommendation: Move per-operation formatting into the operation definition itself (e.g., op.cliHints.format?: (result) => string). The CLI then becomes a generic dispatcher: `const out = op.cliHints?.format?.(result) ?? JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)`. This co-locates result shape and presentation, eliminating the god-switch.

findings.title: Resolver SDK exports internal _resetDefaultRegistry helper
findings.description: src/core/resolvers/index.ts exports `_resetDefaultRegistry` through the public SDK barrel. The underscore prefix signals intent (test-only) but exporting it through the same public surface as Resolver/ResolverError invites external consumers to depend on it, freezing test infrastructure as a stability commitment.
findings.recommendation: Move test helpers to a separate barrel (e.g., src/core/resolvers/testing.ts) that's not part of the documented SDK surface. Or use __testing pattern already used elsewhere (agent.ts, agent-logs.ts, apply-migrations.ts).

findings.title: Inconsistent module boundary: engine-factory exposed but PGLite engine class also exported
findings.description: package.json exports both './engine-factory' AND './pglite-engine' AND './engine' as separate entry points. This signals three different consumer paths for engine creation: factory (recommended), direct class instantiation (PGLite), or interface-only. The lack of a single canonical path makes it easy for plugins to bypass the factory and miss config-driven dispatch.
findings.recommendation: Designate one canonical entry: export only './engine-factory' for instantiation and './engine' for the type. Mark direct engine class imports as internal. Update plugin author docs accordingly.

findings.title: Help text duplicated between CLI registry and printHelp string literal
findings.description: printHelp() in cli.ts is a 100+ line string literal listing every command and its description, but cliOps already has descriptions for shared operations. The help text drifts independently from the operation registry and CLI_ONLY set — there's no compile-time check that all commands are documented.
findings.recommendation: Generate help text from the registry: iterate operations + CLI_ONLY commands grouped by category (categories declared on each command spec). Keep only a banner + USAGE/SETUP intro as static text. This makes new commands self-documenting.

findings.title: Minions barrel exports concrete classes alongside types — fine, but no orchestration boundary doc
findings.description: src/core/minions/index.ts cleanly exports MinionQueue, MinionWorker, calculateBackoff and types from a single barrel — this is good. However, the supervisor module is not exported from the barrel even though it's part of the orchestration triad (queue/worker/supervisor). Consumers must reach into ./supervisor directly. Either it's intentionally internal (then document it) or it should join the barrel.
findings.recommendation: Add MinionSupervisor to the barrel if it's part of the public minions API, or add a comment stating it's internal-only and consumers should compose Queue+Worker themselves. Document the orchestration boundaries (who owns lifecycle, retries, child-fail policy) in a brief module-level doc.

findings.title: Migration registry uses static imports, preventing tree-shaking and lazy loading
findings.description: src/commands/migrations/index.ts imports all 11 migrations statically into a single array. Every CLI invocation (even unrelated commands) loads all migration code into memory. Given migrations only run on `apply-migrations`, this is wasted startup cost on the hot CLI path.
findings.recommendation: Convert migrations to a registry of { version, headline, load: () => Promise<Migration> } entries. Lazy-load only when apply-migrations runs. Keeps the registry as the source of truth without paying the import cost on every CLI startup.

findings.title: Auth `test` subcommand argument parsing flaw allows token leak via process listing
findings.description: In `runAuth`, the `test` subcommand parses `--token` by index, but the URL detection `rest.find(a => !a.startsWith('--') && a !== rest[tokenIdx + 1])` may misidentify the URL when arguments are reordered, potentially passing the token as URL or vice versa. More importantly, tokens supplied on the command line are visible to other users via `ps`/`/proc`. CWE-214: Invocation of Process Using Visible Sensitive Information.
findings.recommendation: Read the token from an environment variable (e.g., GBRAIN_TOKEN) or stdin instead of a CLI flag, and warn users that --token may leak via process tables. Also tighten arg parsing to deterministically identify the URL positional.

findings.title: Token created without expiration / rotation policy
findings.description: `access_tokens` rows have `created_at` and `revoked_at` but no expiration timestamp. Long-lived bearer tokens that never auto-expire elevate the blast radius of any leak. CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration. OWASP A07:2021.
findings.recommendation: Add an `expires_at` column with a sensible default (e.g., 90 days), enforce it in the auth-validation path, and surface remaining lifetime in `auth list`. Consider supporting rotation via `auth rotate <name>`.

findings.title: Token printed to stdout (may be captured by shell history / logs)
findings.description: `auth create` prints the generated token via `console.log`, which gets captured in shell history (when piped/teed), CI logs, and terminal scrollback. CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File.
findings.recommendation: Offer `--output-file <path>` writing with 0600 perms, or write to stderr with a clear note. At minimum, add a warning in the printed message instructing users to clear their terminal/shell history.

findings.title: Lock file race between stat and write in autopilot
findings.description: The autopilot lock-file logic does a stat-then-write without atomic exclusivity. Two concurrent `gbrain autopilot` invocations can both pass the freshness check and both write their PID, defeating mutual exclusion. CWE-367: TOCTOU Race Condition.
findings.recommendation: Use `fs.openSync(lockPath, 'wx')` (exclusive create) or a real OS file lock (`flock`/`lockfile-utils`). On EEXIST, check mtime to detect stale locks then delete-and-retry once.

findings.title: Unbounded JSON parse on user-supplied tool args (`gbrain call`)
findings.description: `runCall` calls `JSON.parse(jsonStr)` directly on argv with no size cap, schema check, or prototype-pollution guard. A maliciously crafted argument like `'{"__proto__":{"polluted":true}}'` mutates Object.prototype globally for the process. CWE-1321: Prototype Pollution. CWE-20: Improper Input Validation.
findings.recommendation: Use a safe parser (e.g., `JSON.parse` with a reviver that drops `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` keys) or schema-validate against the operation's `params` definition before passing to the handler. Cap argv length (e.g., 1MB).

findings.title: MCP stdio handler trusts caller-supplied params without rate limiting
findings.description: `startMcpServer` dispatches every CallToolRequest with `remote: true` but applies no per-session rate limit, concurrency cap, or payload-size limit at the stdio layer. A misbehaving MCP client can flood the dispatcher and exhaust DB connections. CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling.
findings.recommendation: Add a minimal in-process token bucket (e.g., 50 req/s per session) and enforce a max param-payload size in `dispatchToolCall`. Even stdio clients can be misconfigured loops.

findings.title: Files not visible in plan: shell handler, brain-allowlist, MCP rate-limiter, storage modules
findings.description: The PLAN identifies `src/core/minions/handlers/shell.ts`, `shell-audit.ts`, `brain-allowlist.ts`, `mcp/http-transport.ts`, `mcp/rate-limit.ts`, `mcp/dispatch.ts`, `core/storage/s3.ts`, `core/storage/supabase.ts`, `core/supabase-admin.ts`, `core/config.ts`, `core/resolvers/builtin/x-api/handle-to-tweet.ts`, `.gitleaks.toml`, `test/file-upload-security.test.ts`, `test/query-sanitization.test.ts`, and `SECURITY.md` as the focus areas, but only file listings (not source) for those were provided. Findings on those concerns (command injection in shell handler, MCP HTTP auth, S3/Supabase authz, query sanitization, brain allowlist enforcement) cannot be made without the source.
findings.recommendation: Re-run the security scan with the full source for the planned files attached. Until then, treat this as a coverage gap rather than a clean bill of health for those modules.

findings.title: Pervasive use of 'any' type undermines TypeScript strictness
findings.description: Despite TypeScript usage, the codebase contains numerous `as any` casts and `: any` type annotations in critical paths (cli.ts formatResult, mcp/server.ts request handlers, autopilot.ts engine probes, auth.ts error handling). This defeats the value of TypeScript's type system, particularly in the CLI output formatter where every result branch casts to `any`, losing type safety on user-facing output shapes.
findings.recommendation: Define explicit result types for each operation (GetPageResult, ListPagesResult, etc.) and replace `as any` casts with proper type narrowing. For MCP SDK width issues, create a local typed interface rather than casting to any.

findings.title: Massive command dispatcher in cli.ts violates single responsibility
findings.description: The handleCliOnly function in cli.ts is approximately 230 lines containing 30+ if/switch branches for command dispatch, each duplicating the dynamic-import pattern. This is a textbook God Function: high cyclomatic complexity (~30+), difficult to test, and adding/removing commands requires touching this file plus the CLI_ONLY Set declared 200 lines earlier (easy to drift).
findings.recommendation: Extract to a command registry pattern: `commandRegistry.register({ name, needsEngine, lazyImport })`. Drive both CLI_ONLY membership and dispatch from one source of truth. Cuts ~200 lines and eliminates the registration/dispatch drift risk.

findings.title: CLI_ONLY command list duplicated as inline Set, drifts from dispatcher
findings.description: The CLI_ONLY Set at line 22 lists 40+ command names as a single literal array, separate from the switch/if dispatcher in handleCliOnly. There's no compile-time guarantee these stay in sync — a command added to dispatch but not the Set will fall through to operations lookup with confusing errors. The 'reconcile-links' command is in the dispatcher (line 414) but is NOT in the CLI_ONLY Set on line 22.
findings.recommendation: Derive CLI_ONLY from the registry described above. Add a unit test that asserts every dispatched command is registered.

findings.title: Duplicated subagent data construction in agent.ts fanout path
findings.description: In runFanout (src/commands/agent.ts), the SubagentHandlerData object construction is duplicated verbatim between the single-entry short-circuit and the N-entry loop (~12 lines each). This violates DRY and any future field added to subagent submission must be edited in both places.
findings.recommendation: Extract `buildSubagentData(entry, flags, promptTemplate): SubagentHandlerData` and call it from both branches. Same for the `submitOpts` construction.

findings.title: Dead/unreachable code in code-def.ts
findings.description: In runCodeDef, line 88 computes `const symbol = args.find(...)` but the value is never used — the next line recomputes via `positional[0]`. The unused `symbol` binding is leftover from a refactor.
findings.recommendation: Remove the unused `symbol` constant. Add `noUnusedLocals: true` to tsconfig.json to prevent recurrence.

findings.title: Near-identical code-callers and code-callees commands invite drift
findings.description: src/commands/code-callers.ts and src/commands/code-callees.ts are ~70 lines each and nearly byte-identical except for the engine method called and a few labels. Bugfixes must be applied twice; behavior can diverge silently.
findings.recommendation: Extract a shared `runCallGraphQuery(engine, args, { method: 'callers'|'callees', label })` function. Each command file becomes a thin adapter (~15 lines).

findings.title: Inconsistent flag parsing logic duplicated across commands
findings.description: `parseFlag(args, name)` is reimplemented in agent.ts, agent-logs.ts (parseSince), apply-migrations.ts, autopilot.ts, code-def.ts, code-callers.ts, code-callees.ts — at least 6+ copies of the same `args.indexOf(flag)` pattern. Each variant has minor differences (some support `=`, some don't). check-resolvable.ts has yet another flag parser. This guarantees inconsistent CLI UX.
findings.recommendation: Extract a single `src/core/cli-args.ts` with `parseFlag`, `parseFlagInt`, `hasFlag`, `parsePositionals`. Migrate all commands. Add tests for `--key=value`, `--key value`, and `--no-key` forms.

findings.title: Inconsistent error handling: process.exit + console.error vs OperationError envelope
findings.description: src/core/errors.ts apparently provides errorFor/serializeError envelopes (used in code-def, code-callers, code-callees) but most commands use raw `console.error` + `process.exit(1)`: auth.ts, autopilot.ts, agent.ts, apply-migrations.ts, backlinks.ts, check-update.ts. This gives agents two completely different error contracts (JSON envelope vs plain stderr) depending on which command they hit.
findings.recommendation: Standardize all CLI commands on the errors.ts envelope. Provide a `runWithErrorEnvelope(handler, { json })` wrapper that handles JSON-vs-human output uniformly. Add lint rule against bare `process.exit` outside the wrapper.

findings.title: Silent error swallowing via empty catch blocks
findings.description: Multiple `catch { /* best-effort */ }` and `catch { /* swallow */ }` blocks across autopilot.ts (~12 instances), apply-migrations.ts, and agent.ts. While 'best-effort' filesystem ops are valid, these blocks hide real failures during debugging. Particularly concerning: apply-migrations.ts:300 swallows ledger-write failure on the throw path with no logging — exactly the silent-drift scenario the comments elsewhere warn against.
findings.recommendation: Replace `catch {}` with `catch (e) { logError('phase', e); }` using the existing logError helper. At minimum log to ~/.gbrain/*.log so post-mortem debugging works. The ledger-write swallow on throw path should at least append to a separate failure log.

findings.title: Long function with high complexity: runAutopilot
findings.description: src/commands/autopilot.ts:runAutopilot is ~250 lines with worker spawn, lock file handling, signal handlers, dispatch loop, peer-liveness probe, health check, adaptive interval, and shutdown logic all interleaved. Cyclomatic complexity is high (>15 branches), and the function is impossible to unit-test in pieces. Comments throughout reveal accreted bug fixes (Codex C, B7, fix patterns) that suggest the function has grown organically.
findings.recommendation: Extract: `acquireLock()`, `spawnManagedWorker(cliPath)`, `dispatchOneCycle(engine, mode)`, `runPeerLivenessProbe(engine)`, `runAdaptiveSleep(score, base)`. Each extraction unblocks unit testing. Aim for runAutopilot ≤60 lines as an orchestrator.

findings.title: Long function with high complexity: runApplyMigrations
findings.description: runApplyMigrations is ~150 lines with arg parsing, first-install guard, force-retry handling, schema-version pre-flight, plan building, wedged warnings, and a per-migration loop with nested try/catch and ledger writes. The pre-flight DB connection block (lines 226-247) does its own engine lifecycle inline which duplicates connectEngine logic.
findings.recommendation: Extract `preflightSchemaCheck()`, `runOneMigration(m, opts)`, and `recordOutcome(m, result)`. The migration loop body should be ~10 lines invoking these.

findings.title: Magic numbers without named constants
findings.description: Several magic numbers appear inline: `5_000_000` (cli.ts stdin cap), `35_000` (autopilot shutdown grace), `5 * 60 * 1000` (STABLE_RUN_RESET_MS — at least named), `2048` (RSS watchdog MB), `300_000` (timeout floor), `24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (default agent timeout). These hinder maintainability and readers can't tell intent.
findings.recommendation: Hoist to module-level constants: `const WORKER_RSS_LIMIT_MB = 2048;`, `const SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS = 35_000;`, `const STDIN_MAX_BYTES = 5_000_000;`. Group related constants in a `constants.ts` per module.

findings.title: Inline deprecation warning printed to stderr without versioning policy
findings.description: src/cli.ts:469 prints a deprecation notice for `repos` → `sources` on every invocation with no opt-out mechanism, no removal version, and no log level. Long-running CI scripts will accumulate noise.
findings.recommendation: Add a removal version (`removed in v0.25.0`), respect `GBRAIN_QUIET_DEPRECATIONS=1`, and route through a single `deprecate(feature, since, until)` helper for consistent UX across future deprecations.

findings.title: Argument parsing in runAuth test branch is fragile
findings.description: In auth.ts:runAuth, `const url = rest.find(a => !a.startsWith('--') && a !== rest[tokenIdx + 1])` tries to find the URL by exclusion of the token argument. This breaks if the URL happens to equal the token, and `tokenIdx + 1` indexing is undefined when `--token` is absent (tokenIdx = -1, accessing rest[0]). The check on line 246-247 catches missing values but the `find()` logic is unnecessarily brittle.
findings.recommendation: Use proper positional/flag separation: walk args, treating `--token <val>` as a flag pair and the first non-flag positional as the URL. Or use a small parser module (see DRY finding above).

findings.title: Documentation files referenced in plan are not provided for review
findings.description: The analysis plan calls for review of README.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/, skills/, and recipes/, but only their filenames appear in the listing — actual content is not included. Findings below are limited to inline source documentation; a full documentation audit cannot be completed without the markdown content.
findings.recommendation: Re-run the documentation audit with the actual contents of README.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md, and docs/skills/recipes directories included so SKILL.md conformance, migration guide completeness, and MCP deploy/integration accuracy can be verified.

findings.title: CLI help text duplicates command list, drifts from CLI_ONLY registry
findings.description: printHelp() in src/cli.ts hard-codes a long usage block while the CLI_ONLY set and per-command handlers are the actual source of truth. Several commands listed in CLI_ONLY (e.g. 'skillpack-check', 'skillpack', 'resolvers', 'integrity', 'repair-jsonb', 'orphans', 'sources', 'reindex-code', 'apply-migrations', 'frontmatter') have no entry or only partial mentions in the help text, and 'reconcile-links' is implemented in the switch but absent from CLI_ONLY entirely. This will cause user-facing help to diverge from reality on every release.
findings.recommendation: Generate the help block from the operations registry + a structured CLI_ONLY metadata table (name, group, summary). At minimum, add an automated test that asserts every command in CLI_ONLY and every cliOps entry appears in printHelp() output. Also fix the missing 'reconcile-links' entry in CLI_ONLY.

findings.title: 'reconcile-links' command implemented but missing from CLI_ONLY allowlist
findings.description: src/cli.ts handleCliOnly() includes a 'case reconcile-links' branch with substantive comments, but 'reconcile-links' is not in the CLI_ONLY Set on line 25. As written, the dispatcher will reject the command before reaching the switch, meaning the documented behavior is unreachable. This is both a bug and a documentation/discoverability issue: the command is undocumented in --help and unusable.
findings.recommendation: Add 'reconcile-links' to the CLI_ONLY set, and add a corresponding line in printHelp() under the CODE INDEXING section (which already documents 'reconcile-links [--dry-run]' but the command itself is unreachable).

findings.title: Migration registry lacks documentation of skipped versions
findings.description: src/commands/migrations/index.ts registers migrations v0_11_0 through v0_22_4 but skips v0.15.x, v0.17.x, v0.19.x, v0.20.x explicitly (v0_14_0 → v0_16_0 → v0_18_0 → v0_18_1 → v0_21_0 → v0_22_4). The module docstring does not explain why these versions are absent — were they no-op upgrades, rolled into adjacent migrations, or was the registry pruned? Migration guide completeness is a stated concern in the analysis plan.
findings.recommendation: Expand the module-level JSDoc to (a) document the version-skip policy (e.g. 'only versions requiring orchestrator action are listed; v0.15/v0.17/v0.19/v0.20 were schema-only and run via initSchema'), and (b) cross-reference skills/migrations/vX.Y.Z.md for the host-agent narrative. Consider an inline comment next to gaps like `// v0.15-v0.17: schema-only, no orchestrator`.

findings.title: MCP server module lacks usage and security documentation
findings.description: src/mcp/server.ts exports startMcpServer and handleToolCall but provides only inline cast-explanation comments. There is no module-level docstring describing transport options (stdio vs HTTP — referenced in dispatch.ts comments), the trusted-vs-remote security boundary, how to wire the server to Claude Desktop / clawhub, or what 'remote=true' implies for callers. The plan flags 'MCP deploy/integration docs accuracy' as a concern.
findings.recommendation: Add a module header explaining: (1) supported transports, (2) the remote/trusted distinction and which tools are gated, (3) example client config snippet, (4) link to the MCP integration guide in docs/. Also add JSDoc to the two exported functions describing parameters and the response envelope shape.

findings.title: core/index.ts and minions/index.ts barrels lack module documentation
findings.description: src/core/index.ts and src/core/minions/index.ts are public-API barrel files (referenced from package.json 'exports') but have no module-level JSDoc explaining what consumers should import from each entry point. By contrast, src/core/resolvers/index.ts and src/core/output/validators/index.ts include helpful module headers — the inconsistency suggests the docs were never backfilled.
findings.recommendation: Add a brief module header to each barrel file (3-5 lines) describing: (a) which package.json export path it corresponds to, (b) what subset of the API it surfaces, (c) which import path consumers should prefer. Mirror the pattern already used in resolvers/index.ts.

findings.title: formatResult uses 'as any' casts without documenting result shapes
findings.description: formatResult() in src/cli.ts dispatches on operation name and casts results to 'any' (e.g. `const r = result as any` on get_page, `const s = result as any` on get_stats, `const h = result as any` on get_health). The expected fields (compiled_truth, frontmatter, page_count, embed_coverage, link_coverage, etc.) are not documented anywhere in this file, making it impossible for a contributor to know which operation contracts the formatter relies on. The health-score weights comment is helpful but isolated.
findings.recommendation: Replace 'as any' with imported result types from src/core/operations.ts (or wherever the operation result types live). If type imports are impractical, add a JSDoc @typedef block at the top of formatResult listing each handled opName and its expected result shape, plus link to where the canonical type lives.

findings.title: package.json postinstall hook lacks documentation of failure semantics
findings.description: The postinstall script `command -v gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 && gbrain apply-migrations --yes --non-interactive || echo '[gbrain] postinstall skipped...'` has subtle semantics: if `gbrain` exists on PATH, apply-migrations runs and a non-zero exit would normally fail the install — but the `||` swallows it. There is no comment explaining intent, which behaviors are intentional, or how this interacts with the first-install guard in apply-migrations.ts. Issue #218 is referenced but the user-facing rationale is buried.
findings.recommendation: Move the postinstall logic into scripts/postinstall.sh with inline comments explaining: (1) why `command -v` precedes execution, (2) why failures are swallowed (don't break `bun install`), (3) the relationship to first-install-guard in apply-migrations.ts. Reference the script from package.json. This also makes the behavior testable.

findings.title: auth.ts dual-entry-point design only partially documented
findings.description: src/commands/auth.ts can be invoked as both a CLI subcommand (`gbrain auth ...`) and a standalone script (`bun run src/commands/auth.ts ...`). The header comment mentions both modes, but the `test` subcommand's argument-parsing logic is convoluted (`rest.find(a => !a.startsWith('--') && a !== rest[tokenIdx + 1])`) without a JSDoc explaining the precedence rules or example invocations. The standalone-script messaging in `create()` ('Revoke with: bun run src/commands/auth.ts revoke ...') is wrong when invoked via `gbrain auth create`.
findings.recommendation: (1) Detect invocation mode (import.meta.main vs CLI dispatch) and surface the correct revoke command in the success message. (2) Add a JSDoc to the test() function showing canonical invocation: `gbrain auth test https://example.com/mcp --token gbrain_...`. (3) Document the test-arg-parsing rule in a comment.

findings.title: Long inline comments substitute for missing dedicated docs
findings.description: Several files carry multi-paragraph inline comments that read like missing markdown docs — e.g., autopilot.ts shutdown semantics (lines ~165-170), autopilot.ts no-worker probe rationale (~280-290), apply-migrations.ts Bug 3 wedged-migration semantics (lines ~95-130), check-resolvable.ts deferred-checks history (~50-60). These are valuable but buried; readers need the architectural context before reading the code. The plan calls for review of docs/, suggesting this material should live there.
findings.recommendation: Extract architecture-level comments (autopilot supervisor lifecycle, migration ledger semantics, resolver health exit codes) into docs/architecture/*.md and replace the inline blocks with a one-line summary + link. Keep per-line implementation rationale inline. This makes onboarding faster and prevents the docs-vs-code drift that plain inline comments invite.

findings.title: code-def/code-callers/code-callees CLI flags inconsistently documented
findings.description: All three commands accept `--limit`, `--source`, `--all-sources`, `--json`/`--no-json`, and code-def adds `--lang`. The help/error hints embedded via errorFor() differ slightly across files (e.g. code-def hint shows `[--lang <language>] [--json]` but omits `--limit` and `--source`; code-callers/callees hints show `[--all-sources] [--limit N] [--json]` but omit `--source`). printHelp() in cli.ts also doesn't list `--all-sources` or `--source` for these commands.
findings.recommendation: Standardize the usage hint string across code-def/code-refs/code-callers/code-callees to list all supported flags consistently, and update printHelp() in cli.ts to mention `--all-sources` and `--source` for code-callers/callees. Consider extracting a shared `CODE_QUERY_FLAGS_HINT` constant.

findings.title: DEFERRED array kept as 'stable public field' but no API contract documented
findings.description: src/commands/check-resolvable.ts exports DEFERRED as an empty array with a comment 'export stays as a stable public field of the --json envelope so downstream consumers that check `.deferred[]` keep working.' However, the JSON envelope's stability contract is not documented anywhere visible — no schema file, no docs/api/ reference, no version note. Downstream consumers have no canonical place to learn what fields are guaranteed.
findings.recommendation: Document the Envelope interface as a stable JSON contract in docs/api/check-resolvable.md (or similar), including a versioned schema. Add a JSDoc @stable tag (or equivalent) to the Envelope interface. List `deferred` and `error` enum values explicitly.

findings.title: agent.ts printHelp omits --no-follow flag that the parser accepts
findings.description: parseRunFlags() in src/commands/agent.ts accepts `--no-follow` (line ~117), but the help text printed by printHelp() lists only `--follow` and `--detach`. Users reading `gbrain agent run --help` won't discover `--no-follow`, even though the parser explicitly handles it.
findings.recommendation: Add `--no-follow` to the SUBMITTING section of printHelp() with a one-line description (e.g. 'Submit and exit immediately even on a TTY'). Also clarify how it interacts with `--detach`.

findings.title: Strong inline-doc patterns present but coverage is uneven
findings.description: Positive note: many files demonstrate excellent documentation discipline — agent-logs.ts, apply-migrations.ts, autopilot.ts, check-resolvable.ts, and migrations/index.ts all have substantive module headers explaining purpose, invocation paths, and design rationale. Comments often cite version numbers (v0.11.1, v0.18, v0.20.0 Cathedral II) and bug IDs (Bug 3, Codex H9), giving readers historical context. However, simpler command files (call.ts, code-def.ts) and barrel files (core/index.ts, minions/index.ts) lack equivalent headers, creating an uneven reader experience.
findings.recommendation: Establish a 'minimum module header' template (5-10 lines: purpose, public API, invocation example, related skills/migration version) and enforce it via a lint rule or CONTRIBUTING.md checklist for any file under src/commands/ or src/core/.

findings.title: tree-sitter-wasms pinned to old 0.1.13 with no upgrade strategy
findings.description: tree-sitter-wasms is pinned exactly to 0.1.13 (no caret, no range). This is a supply-chain-sensitive package that ships pre-built WASM grammars. While exact pinning is appropriate for WASM provenance (matches the check-wasm-embedded.sh test script reference), there's no documented upgrade or verification policy and the version is well behind current releases (0.1.x line has had multiple releases). Combined with web-tree-sitter 0.22.6 (also exactly pinned), the grammar runtime + grammar artifacts are frozen and may miss security/parser fixes.
findings.recommendation: Document the WASM pinning strategy in a SECURITY.md or PROVENANCE.md, generate SHA-256 checksums for embedded .wasm files, and establish a quarterly review cadence to bump tree-sitter-wasms and web-tree-sitter together. Consider scripts/check-wasm-embedded.sh to also verify hashes, not just presence.

findings.title: @electric-sql/pglite pinned to 0.4.3 — major version line moves quickly
findings.description: @electric-sql/pglite is pinned exactly to 0.4.3 and listed in trustedDependencies (runs install scripts). PGLite is pre-1.0 and ships frequent fixes including data-integrity and WASM-loader patches. Exact-pin combined with elevated install-script trust means CVE remediation requires a manual bump.
findings.recommendation: Subscribe to @electric-sql/pglite release notes, set up Renovate/Dependabot with a dedicated rule for this package (auto-PR but require manual merge given trustedDependencies status), and verify each bump with the existing typecheck + smoke-test pipeline.

findings.title: Caret ranges on security-critical SDKs allow silent drift
findings.description: @anthropic-ai/sdk ^0.30.0, @aws-sdk/client-s3 ^3.1028.0, openai ^4.0.0, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.0.0, and postgres ^3.4.0 all use caret ranges. These are auth/network/data-egress packages where a transient resolution change between developer machines and CI without lockfile enforcement could ship subtly different behavior. The `bun.lock` file is present (good), but `bun install --frozen-lockfile` does not appear to be enforced in any script.
findings.recommendation: Add `bun install --frozen-lockfile` to CI (test script or a dedicated check). Consider tightening @modelcontextprotocol/sdk from `^1.0.0` (extremely permissive — accepts 1.x.x) to a narrower range like `^1.5.0` or pin to current resolved version.

findings.title: @types/bun: latest — non-deterministic builds
findings.description: `"@types/bun": "latest"` in devDependencies resolves to whatever is current at install time. While the lockfile pins the actual resolved version, this is an anti-pattern that defeats reproducibility for any contributor running `bun install` after lockfile drift, and signals to tools that any version is acceptable. Type definition changes in @types/bun regularly cause typecheck failures (the `npm run test` pipeline runs `tsc --noEmit`).
findings.recommendation: Replace `"latest"` with the currently-resolved version from bun.lock (e.g., `"^1.x.y"` matching the Bun runtime version). Pin both @types/bun and the implied Bun runtime in package.json's `engines` field.

findings.title: Missing engines field — no Bun version constraint
findings.description: The project uses Bun-specific features (`bun build --compile`, bunfig.toml, `#!/usr/bin/env bun` shebangs) but package.json has no `engines` field. Users running an incompatible Bun version may hit cryptic errors. The `build:all` script targets `bun-darwin-arm64` and `bun-linux-x64` which only exist in recent Bun versions.
findings.recommendation: Add `"engines": { "bun": ">=1.1.0" }` (or whatever minimum is actually required) and document the supported range in README. Consider also a runtime check at the top of cli.ts.

findings.title: postinstall hook silently swallows migration errors
findings.description: The postinstall hook `command -v gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 && gbrain apply-migrations --yes --non-interactive || echo '...'` runs migrations on install but suppresses ALL errors via `||` fallback. A failed migration during `bun install -g github:...` produces only a one-line warning to stderr. This is a supply-chain risk: a malicious or buggy migration could fail silently while the install reports success. The hint URL also goes to a specific issue (#218) which may not be the right destination forever.
findings.recommendation: Make postinstall failure visible: log to ~/.gbrain/postinstall.log, print a clearer warning, and consider gating apply-migrations behind an env var (GBRAIN_SKIP_POSTINSTALL_MIGRATE=1) for CI/automation. Also avoid hardcoding GitHub issue numbers in user-facing error text.

findings.title: Trusted dependencies includes only @electric-sql/pglite — verify install scripts intent
findings.description: `trustedDependencies: ["@electric-sql/pglite"]` correctly limits which packages can run install scripts under Bun. This is a positive supply-chain control. However, no SBOM or audit policy is documented to justify why this specific package is trusted, and there's no signal of periodic review of the trust list.
findings.recommendation: Document the trustedDependencies rationale in CONTRIBUTING.md or SECURITY.md (e.g., 'pglite needs install scripts to fetch its WASM artifact'). Establish a quarterly review of the list. Consider adding a CI check that fails if new entries are added without review.

findings.title: openclaw plugin compat range too permissive
findings.description: `"openclaw": { "compat": { "pluginApi": ">=2026.4.0" } }` declares compatibility with any future plugin API version. Using `>=` without an upper bound means a breaking 2027.x or 2030.x plugin API change would still match this declaration, leading to runtime failures rather than install-time rejection.
findings.recommendation: Use a bounded range like `>=2026.4.0 <2027.0.0` or follow the plugin API ecosystem's recommended pinning scheme to fail fast on incompatible host versions.

findings.title: Performance analysis files referenced in PLAN are not provided
findings.description: The PLAN identifies critical performance-sensitive files (queue.ts, worker.ts, supervisor.ts, hybrid.ts, two-pass.ts, sql-ranking.ts, vector.ts, embedding.ts, semantic.ts, code.ts, backoff.ts) but the analyzed_code section only contains CLI/command wrappers (cli.ts, agent.ts, autopilot.ts, backlinks.ts, etc.). The actual implementation of queue throughput, backpressure, hybrid search, and embedding batching cannot be assessed from the provided code.
findings.recommendation: Re-run the analysis with the actual core/minions/ and core/search/ source files included. The CLI files alone do not expose the algorithmic hot paths.

findings.title: Synchronous filesystem walk for backlink scanning blocks event loop on large brains
findings.description: findBacklinkGaps() performs a recursive synchronous walk using readdirSync/lstatSync/readFileSync, then loads every .md file into memory simultaneously. For a 50K-page brain (mentioned in the comment), this loads potentially hundreds of MB into a single allPages array and blocks the event loop for seconds. The heartbeat comment acknowledges 'On 50K-page brains that can take seconds' but does not address the underlying O(N) memory allocation or blocking I/O.
findings.recommendation: Convert to async fs.promises with a streaming/chunked approach: process files in batches of 500-1000, release content references after extracting refs, and use fs.opendir for streaming directory iteration. Consider building pagesBySlug index in a first pass without holding content, then stream content per-target during gap detection.

findings.title: Backlinks CLI re-walks brain directory after core scan
findings.description: runBacklinks() calls runBacklinksCore() which performs the full findBacklinkGaps() walk, then for the 'check' action calls findBacklinkGaps(brainDir) AGAIN to render details. On a 50K-page brain this doubles the I/O and CPU cost of the check command for purely cosmetic output formatting.
findings.recommendation: Have runBacklinksCore return the gaps array (not just counts) so the CLI can render details without a second walk. Alternatively, pipe gaps through the result envelope.

findings.title: Polling loop in agent logs uses fixed 1s interval with no backoff
findings.description: dumpSince() is called every 1000ms (default pollMs) for the entire lifetime of a --follow session. Each poll executes readSubagentAuditForJob (filesystem JSONL read), loadTranscriptRows (DB query), and readJobStatus (DB query). For long-running jobs (24h timeout default) this generates ~86,400 DB round trips per follow session even when the job is idle.
findings.recommendation: Implement exponential backoff or adaptive polling: start at 500ms, double up to 5-10s when no new events are seen, reset to fast polling on activity. Alternatively, use LISTEN/NOTIFY on minion_jobs status changes to event-drive the loop.

findings.title: Health check + reconnect attempt every autopilot cycle adds DB load
findings.description: The autopilot loop runs engine.getConfig('version') as a health probe every cycle (default 300s, but adaptive down to 60s) and engine.getHealth() for adaptive interval calculation. getHealth() typically computes coverage stats across pages/embeddings — running it every minute on a degraded brain produces continuous load.
findings.recommendation: Cache health score for at least 5 minutes regardless of cycle interval. Skip the version probe when the previous cycle succeeded (use a 'last successful query' timestamp).

findings.title: Crash-restart counter resets aggressively, masking sustained worker instability
findings.description: The autopilot worker supervisor resets crashCount to 1 (not 0) when a worker survives >5 minutes (STABLE_RUN_RESET_MS). Combined with a 5-crash give-up threshold and 10s restart delay, a worker that crashes every ~5.5 minutes will run indefinitely without triggering the give-up safeguard. This may mask a degraded production state where the worker is barely stable.
findings.recommendation: Track crashes per rolling window (e.g., 5 crashes in 1 hour triggers give-up) instead of binary stable/unstable reset. Emit a warning metric when crashCount stays >0 for extended periods.

findings.title: fixBacklinkGaps re-reads target file per group but does in-memory string concatenation in a loop
findings.description: For each target page with multiple gaps, the code does repeated content.split('## Timeline'), string.match, and content.slice() concatenations inside the inner loop. With N gaps for one target, this is O(N * file_size) string allocation. For a hub entity referenced by 100 pages, that's 100 full-content rewrites in memory before a single writeFileSync.
findings.recommendation: Compute all backlink entries first, then do a single insertion with one slice/concat operation. Use array push + join('') instead of repeated string concatenation.

cross_cutting_insights: arch-000, qual-001, qual-002, doc-001, arch-009 all converge on the CLI dispatcher/registry drift problem — a single command-registry refactor would resolve all five.
arch-002, arch-003 form a layering pair: dispatch.ts should move to core/, MCP server should only handle transport, and commands/call.ts should consume core/dispatch.ts. Single coordinated refactor.

arch-004, arch-005, qual-000 all point to BrainEngine being under-specified as a port; tightening the interface (adding executeRaw, connect, getHealth, getConfig, getCallersOf, getCalleesOf) would eliminate `as any` casts and let auth.ts route through the engine.
doc-002 is simultaneously a documentation issue AND a functional bug (qual-002 / arch-000) — reconcile-links is unreachable because of the same drift problem.
sec-000 and qual-014 describe the same fragile arg parsing in auth.ts test subcommand from different angles — security and quality both benefit from a shared CLI parser (qual-006).
dep-002, dep-005, dep-006 together describe a reproducibility hygiene gap — adding `engines` field, pinning @types/bun, and CI frozen-lockfile enforcement form a single hardening initiative.
doc-007 and dep-007 are the same postinstall concern from doc and dependency angles — extracting to scripts/postinstall.sh with logging addresses both.
qual-006 (duplicated parseFlag) is upstream of doc-010 and doc-012 (inconsistent/missing flag docs) — a unified parser would let help text be generated from declarations.
